<margin>
<note>This carries the sense of drawing someone in.</note>
</margin>
Zilu <note>a prominent disciple of Confucius</note> requested to go and call for him. Confucius said, "Enough! He knows that I <note>referred to by his personal name, Qiu</note> have fixed my attention on him, and he knows I am traveling to the state of Chu. He suspects that I will certainly cause the King of Chu to summon him. He views me as a sycophant <term>ningren</term> <gloss>a person of glib, flattering speech</gloss>.
<margin>
<note>He also knows that Qiu knows him. This is a stylistic literary technique.</note>
</margin>
<margin>
<note>A stylistic literary technique.</note>
</margin>
If that is the case, a man like him would be ashamed even to hear the words of a sycophant, let alone see such a person face to face. Why do you think he would still be there?" Zilu went to check, but the room was empty.
<margin>
<note>He took his wife and left.</note>
</margin>
<margin>
<note>A place name; an official who guards the borders.</note>
</margin>
<margin>
<note>Mu was a disciple of Confucius.</note>
</margin>
The border-guard of Changwu asked Zimu, saying: "When you handle the affairs of government, do not be reckless <term>lumang</term> <gloss>careless and crude</gloss>; in your governing of the people, do not be superficial <term>mielie</term> <gloss>neglectful and slapdash</gloss>. Formerly...
<margin>
<note>The clods of earth are large and the grass roots are thick.</note>
</margin>
<margin>
<note>The State of Lu.</note>
</margin>
<margin>
<note>Perhaps a good species of plant, or the place where the ground-skin </note><note>the weed Kochia</note> grows.
</margin>

<summary>Confucius explains to Zilu that a hermit has fled to avoid being treated as a political tool, accurately predicting the man's desire for isolation. The narrative then shifts to a border-guard advising Zimu on the importance of careful, thorough governance.</summary>
<keywords>Confucius, Zilu, Chu, sycophancy, Changwu border-guard, Zimu, governance, recklessness</keywords>
